section_summary: This section concerns the four-power division of former Japanese combat vessels, including Soviet and British replies, revised ship inventories, and the disposition of the United States share. It also records French and Australian objections or inquiries, State Department responses, and notice that a Soviet naval representative had departed for Japan.

subfiles.title: Thompson memorandum on Soviet interpretation of ship division
subfiles.about: Suggests wording to counter a possible Soviet claim that a four-power commission should control the division.
subfiles.summary: Recommends deliberately broad acknowledgment of the Soviet note to aid U.S. negotiators.

subfiles.title: Airgram A-36 conveying Soviet note
subfiles.about: Forwards a translation of the Soviet acceptance of dividing Japanese ships.
subfiles.summary: The Soviet Union agrees to send a representative and six aides, proposes four-power arrangements with SCAP, specifies Nakhodka for delivery, and requests information on larger ships.

subfiles.title: Unofficial translation of Soviet Note No. 14
subfiles.about: Accepts immediate ship division and sets out Soviet procedural requests.
subfiles.summary: Requests four-power coordination, delivery at Nakhodka, and information on larger Japanese warships.

subfiles.title: Airgram A-46 transmitting U.S. reply to Soviet note
subfiles.about: Transmits the U.S. answer concerning division and destruction of larger Japanese vessels.
subfiles.summary: Acknowledges Soviet participation and explains that SCAP directives ordered larger surface warships scrapped; detailed information is available from SCAP in Tokyo.

subfiles.title: Cover letter to Secretary of War
subfiles.about: Forwards the U.S. reply to the Soviet Embassy.
subfiles.summary: Encloses the April 25 note answering the Soviet March 10 note.

subfiles.title: U.S. note to Soviet chargé
subfiles.about: Acknowledges Soviet participation and describes the scrapping of larger Japanese warships.
subfiles.summary: Cites SCAPIN 910 and 1002 and directs Soviet requests for details to SCAP headquarters.

subfiles.title: Cover letter to Secretary of the Navy
subfiles.about: Forwards the U.S. reply to the Soviet Embassy.
subfiles.summary: Encloses the April 25 note answering the Soviet March 10 note.

subfiles.title: Duplicate U.S. note to Soviet chargé
subfiles.about: Explains destruction of Japanese surface warships larger than destroyers.
subfiles.summary: States that eligible larger vessels have been or are being scrapped and that SCAP can provide details.

subfiles.title: SWNCC memorandum forwarding revised ship lists
subfiles.about: Submits revised tentative inventories for circulation to the other three powers.
subfiles.summary: SCAP revised the June 1946 lists after casualties, changing conditions, and further investigation. The new lists correct names and numbers, add ships, and change some classifications; they remain subject to revision.

subfiles.title: SWNCC mailing cover
subfiles.about: Identifies the accompanying top-secret material on ship division.
subfiles.summary: Mailing cover for revised ship lists.

subfiles.title: Enclosure A: damaged ex-Japanese ships
subfiles.about: Lists smaller former Japanese combat vessels needing more than 60 days to become operable.
subfiles.summary: A location-based inventory covers destroyers, escorts, patrol craft, auxiliaries, transports, and rescue boats. Its recapitulation totals 221 vessels.

subfiles.title: Enclosure B: operable ships arranged for disposition
subfiles.about: Lists operable former Japanese vessels in four equal lots and a further ungrouped pool.
subfiles.summary: The first two pages assign destroyers and escorts to four equal lots. The third identifies 48 additional available vessels not yet grouped into equal lots.

subfiles.title: Enclosure C: operable or readily repairable ships
subfiles.about: Inventories former Japanese ships operable or repairable within 60 days.
subfiles.summary: The list covers 239 vessels and gives classes, reserve or service status, and explanatory codes. It includes destroyers, escorts, patrol craft, minesweepers, transports, and auxiliaries.

subfiles.title: Note to Soviet chargé transmitting revised lists
subfiles.about: Replaces earlier ship inventories with revised tentative lists.
subfiles.summary: Encloses three revised lists covering damaged vessels, ships in four lots, and ships operable within 60 days. Explains that SCAP's continuing investigations may require further changes.

subfiles.title: Note to British ambassador transmitting revised lists
subfiles.about: Confidentially supplies revised tentative Japanese ship lists.
subfiles.summary: Replaces the June 1946 inventories with three revised enclosures and cautions that SCAP may revise them again.

subfiles.title: Note to Chinese ambassador transmitting revised lists
subfiles.about: Confidentially supplies revised tentative Japanese ship lists.
subfiles.summary: Sends revised enclosures for damaged, allotted, and readily operable ships and notes that the lists remain provisional.

subfiles.title: Instruction 458 forwarding Soviet note
subfiles.about: Sends the Soviet note on division of smaller Japanese combat vessels.
subfiles.summary: Encloses an unofficial translation of Soviet Note No. 14.

subfiles.title: Enclosed translation of Soviet Note No. 14
subfiles.about: Accepts division and names Soviet requirements for the process.
subfiles.summary: Duplicates the translated note on a seven-person delegation, Nakhodka delivery, and larger ships.

subfiles.title: Instruction 295 forwarding SWNCC paper
subfiles.to: Officer in Charge of American Mission, Nanking
subfiles.about: Forwards a policy paper on U.S. ships operated by Japan.
subfiles.summary: Encloses SWNCC 280/1 for information.

subfiles.title: Far Eastern Subcommittee memorandum on British draft reply
subfiles.to: D. W. Jenkins; J. G. K. Miller; Stephen Jurika
subfiles.about: Circulates a draft answer to the British ambassador for working-group review.
subfiles.summary: Sends the draft at Mr. Emerson's request.

subfiles.title: Draft reply to British ambassador on naval auxiliaries
subfiles.about: Answers British questions about tugs and technical ship data.
subfiles.summary: Excludes tugs and harbor craft from combat division and directs technical inquiries to SCAP.

subfiles.title: Vandenberg referral slip
subfiles.about: Refers a constituent's suggestion on Soviet allocation.
subfiles.summary: Forwards the attached letter with the comment, “Not a bad idea.”

subfiles.title: Mills letter on lend-lease ships and Soviet allocation
subfiles.about: Questions transferring Japanese warships to the Soviet Union before lend-lease settlement.
subfiles.summary: Cites press reports of a 239-ship division and urges withholding the Soviet share.

subfiles.title: Reply to Senator Vandenberg
subfiles.about: Explains why Soviet lend-lease issues cannot delay agreed Japanese ship deliveries.
subfiles.summary: The four powers agreed to divide smaller vessels, and SCAP acts for them collectively. Separate Soviet lend-lease negotiations are expected to address U.S.-supplied ships.

subfiles.title: Revised lend-lease paragraph
subfiles.about: Provides alternate wording on forthcoming Soviet lend-lease negotiations.
subfiles.summary: Says disposition of wartime lend-lease ships will be discussed in Washington.

subfiles.title: Alternative closing page of Vandenberg reply
subfiles.about: States that lend-lease settlement should not affect Soviet receipt of Japanese vessels.
subfiles.summary: Draft closing for the Vandenberg response.

subfiles.title: British Embassy note on delivery arrangements
subfiles.about: Sets British preferences for receiving its share of Japanese vessels.
subfiles.summary: Names Singapore as main port, reserves Hong Kong deliveries, requests a crew repatriation ship, and appoints a naval adviser to draw lots.

subfiles.title: Airgram A-43 conveying British note
subfiles.about: Transmits the British delivery and lottery arrangements.
subfiles.summary: Quotes the British Embassy's April 22 note.

subfiles.title: Cover letter to Secretary of the Navy
subfiles.about: Forwards the British ambassador's April 22 note.
subfiles.summary: Advises that its text was also sent to Tokyo.

subfiles.title: Copy of British Embassy note
subfiles.about: States British ship delivery and crew repatriation preferences.
subfiles.summary: Duplicates the note specifying Singapore, possible Hong Kong delivery, and a naval adviser to draw lots.

subfiles.title: Cover letter to Secretary of War
subfiles.about: Forwards the British ambassador's April 22 note.
subfiles.summary: Advises that its text was sent to Tokyo.

subfiles.title: Assistant Secretary routing note
subfiles.about: Directs appropriate action on an attached matter.
subfiles.summary: Notes a suspense date of April 30 and Mr. Conger's status.

subfiles.title: McCoy letter on French inquiry at FEC
subfiles.about: Requests a U.S. explanation of the basis for four-power division of Japanese vessels.
subfiles.summary: Encloses Ambassador Naggiar's remarks and asks for information to give the Far Eastern Commission.

subfiles.title: Excerpt from 55th FEC meeting
subfiles.about: Records Naggiar's request for an explanation of Japanese fleet division.
subfiles.summary: Naggiar questions the relevance of the 1943 Moscow Declaration and asks the Commission to be informed. McCoy supplies the press release and agrees to refer the request to State.

subfiles.title: Further transcript of FEC discussion
subfiles.about: Records the same exchange over the Commission's role in Japanese disarmament.
subfiles.summary: Naggiar seeks the legal and procedural basis of the four-power division. McCoy provides the public statement, Ramishvili responds briefly, and McCoy promises to take the information request to State.

subfiles.title: Hilldring reply to McCoy
subfiles.about: Provides a discretionary answer to the French FEC inquiry.
subfiles.summary: Explains that the four powers agreed after Japan's surrender to destroy larger vessels and divide destroyers and smaller surface ships. Confidentially notes possible transfer of part of the U.S. share to France and discourages initiating FEC discussion.

subfiles.title: Wallner memorandum of conversation with Lacoste
subfiles.about: Records a French request to expedite transfer of German and Japanese ships.
subfiles.summary: Lacoste presses for a legal decision and indicates French interest centers on receiving the promised vessels.

subfiles.title: Baker memorandum on U.S. share
subfiles.about: Reviews proposed priorities for disposing of the U.S. share of Japanese ships.
subfiles.summary: Participants favor French transfer, occupation use, targets, then scrap; a draft SWNCC paper will be revised before further review.

subfiles.title: Draft SWNCC paper on U.S. ship disposition
subfiles.about: Evaluates targets, scrap, and other uses for vessels allotted to the United States.
subfiles.summary: The draft cites steel shortages, Japanese economic needs, naval target requirements, and the lack of crews or funds to hold vessels. It recommends reassessing Navy needs, offering U.S. industry the chance to fund transport for scrapping, and otherwise scrapping ships in Japan.

subfiles.title: SWNCC memorandum requesting British reply
subfiles.about: Requests transmission of approved language answering the British March 6 note.
subfiles.summary: Encloses approved SWNCC 186/26.

subfiles.title: SWNCC approval decision
subfiles.about: Records approval of SWNCC 186/26.
subfiles.summary: States that the committee approved the paper on May 2.

subfiles.title: SWNCC 186/26 circulation note
subfiles.about: Recommends a reply to the British ambassador.
subfiles.summary: Circulates the Far Eastern Subcommittee's draft note for committee consideration.

subfiles.title: Enclosed draft note to British ambassador
subfiles.about: Clarifies treatment of Japanese naval tugs, harbor craft, and salvage vessels.
subfiles.summary: Excludes these vessels from combat division and reparations, reserves them for Japanese recovery, and refers technical questions on other ships to SCAP.

subfiles.title: State Department note to British ambassador
subfiles.about: Answers British questions on Japanese auxiliaries and ship data.
subfiles.summary: States that small ex-naval tugs, harbor craft, and salvage vessels will support Japan's recovery rather than be divided or treated as reparations. Directs requests for further technical data to SCAP in Tokyo.

subfiles.title: Memorandum on demilitarization of distributable ships
subfiles.about: Summarizes SCAP reports that ships for division were demilitarized.
subfiles.summary: Cites SCAP cables and SWNCC 58/9 on destruction of military equipment.

subfiles.title: Instruction 493 forwarding SWNCC papers
subfiles.about: Sends approved economic-policy and Japanese combat-vessel papers.
subfiles.summary: Encloses SWNCC 302/2, 186/25/D, and 186/26.

subfiles.title: Conversation with Australian ambassador Makin
subfiles.about: Records Australia's objection to immediate four-power division of the Japanese fleet.
subfiles.summary: Makin asserts Australia's wartime contribution and asks that division await a peace-treaty conference. Vincent recalls the 1945 four-power agreement; the Secretary agrees to review the matter.

subfiles.title: Conversation with Australian minister Stirling
subfiles.about: Communicates the U.S. refusal to reopen the four-power ship agreement.
subfiles.summary: Hilldring and Vincent acknowledge Australia's concern but explain that altering a longstanding agreement requires the other three powers' consent. Stirling says he will report Secretary Marshall's decision.

subfiles.title: Secretary's correction request
subfiles.about: Requests a change to the first page of an attached conversation memorandum.
subfiles.summary: Asks Vincent to make the marked change and return the original.

subfiles.title: Handwritten correction instruction
subfiles.about: Requests a change to a line in the memorandum.
subfiles.summary: Brief handwritten instruction to revise one line.

subfiles.title: Revised first page of Makin conversation memorandum
subfiles.about: Reprints the opening of the Australian ambassador's objection to fleet division.
subfiles.summary: Adds that the Secretary was unfamiliar with the issue and would look into it.

subfiles.title: Translation of Soviet Note No. 83
subfiles.about: Reports departure of the Soviet representative for Japanese ship allocation.
subfiles.summary: Rear Admiral Stetsenko and six aides have left for Japan to receive and dispatch the Soviet share.

subfiles.title: Russian original of Soviet Note No. 83
subfiles.about: Original-language note corresponding to the translation on page 306.
subfiles.summary: Russian text of the Soviet delegation notification; OCR is largely unreadable.
